recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Handle any future broader Pharmacy review of MedicationDispense status semantics through a later final Applied/Published tracker rather than reopening FHIR-40692.
issue_request: FHIR-40692 asked Pharmacy to evaluate MedicationDispense status codes after comparison with BiologicallyDerivedProductDispense and resolved to update the MedicationDispense status CodeSystem: in-progress should mean ready for pickup, cancelled should mean the product was not and will not be picked up by the patient, and stopped should be replaced by unfulfilled while preserving the lifecycle meaning.
initial_application: Existing Jira-tagged commits in the current branch applied the issue: 9899efa3e6 changed the MedicationDispense status CodeSystem from stopped/Stopped to unfulfilled/Unfulfilled, 16f693d1d7 and f8000b7c6b changed MedicationDispense example status values to unfulfilled, and 4a6179e9e2 updated the MedicationDispense.status short text. The source/fhir.ini medicationdispense entry confirms the inspected files are active build inputs.
additional_context: Pharmacy minutes from 2023-03-27 record the original MedicationDispense and BiologicallyDerivedProductDispense status mapping discussion that led to the tracker. Pharmacy minutes from 2025-11-03 revisited FHIR-40692, discussed the cancelled versus stopped/unfulfilled distinction, and agreed with the applied unfulfilled name change. Later related Jira items FHIR-54366 and FHIR-54372 discuss not-performed reason and timestamp guidance, but neither is an Applied/Published reversal of the FHIR-40692 status code set in this default run scope. A Zulip search found no directly relevant discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active MedicationDispense CodeSystem already defines in-progress as ready for pickup, cancelled as not/never picked up by the patient, and unfulfilled as the status replacing stopped. MedicationDispense.status short text, example status values, mapping exceptions, and the status-codes table agree on unfulfilled, and no authoritative MedicationDispense status code/display/status value still uses stopped.

related_jiras.note: Later Triaged MedicationDispense issue about ambiguity of statuses that indicate not performed; not a final Applied/Published decision and not a reversal of FHIR-40692.
Later Resolved-change-required issue about status/timestamp invariants and mdd-1 warning level; outside the default Applied/Published source-edit scope and does not alter the status code set.
